Main.sentence: Woke is an adjective derived from ___E:African-American English U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_English)___ used since the 1930s or earlier to refer to awareness of ___E:racial prejudice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_prejudice)___ and ___E:discrimination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_discrimination)___ , often in the construction stay woke .
The term acquired political connotations by the 1970s and gained further popularity in the 2010s with the ___E:hashtag U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashtag)___ #staywoke .

Over time, woke came to be used to refer to a broader awareness of ___E:social inequalities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_inequalities)___ such as ___E:sexism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexism)___ and denial of ___E:LGBTQ rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_rights)___ .

Woke has also been used as shorthand for some ideas of the ___E:American Left U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Left)___ involving ___E:identity politics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identity_politics)___ and ___E:social justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_justice)___ , such as ___E:white privilege U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_privilege)___ and ___E:reparations for slavery in the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reparations_for_slavery_in_the_United_States)___ .

During the 2014 ___E:Ferguson protests U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferguson_protests)___ , the phrase stay woke was popularized by ___E:Black Lives Matter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter)___ (BLM) activists seeking to raise awareness about police shootings of African Americans.

After being used on ___E:Black Twitter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Twitter)___ , the term woke was increasingly adopted by ___E:white people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_people)___ to signal their support for ___E:progressive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressivism)___ causes.
The term became popular with ___E:millennials U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennials)___ and members of ___E:Generation Z U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generation_Z)___ .
As its use spread beyond the United States, woke was added to the Oxford English Dictionary in 2017.

By 2019, the term was widely being used ___E:sarcastically U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcastically)___ as a ___E:pejorative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pejorative)___ by the ___E:political right U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_right)___ and some ___E:centrists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centrists)___ , to disparage ___E:leftist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leftist)___ and progressive movements as superficial and insincere ___E:performative activism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performative_activism)___ .

The terms woke-washing and woke capitalism later emerged to criticize businesses and brands who use politically progressive messaging for financial gain. In the mid-2020s, a number of political commentators also announced the appearance of a " ___E:woke right U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woke_right)___ ", meaning supporters of right-wing views using ___E:cancel culture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancel_culture)___ and similar tactics used by left-wing activists to enforce ___E:conservative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative)___ beliefs.
Wake up Ethiopia!
Wake up Africa!
Let us work towards the one glorious end of a free, redeemed and mighty nation. — ___E:Marcus Garvey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Garvey)___ , Philosophy and Opinions (1923)

In some varieties of ___E:African-American English U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_English)___ , woke is used in place of woken , the usual ___E:past participle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Past_participle)___ form of wake .
This has led to the use of woke as an adjective equivalent to awake , which has become mainstream in the United States.

While it is not known when being awake was first used as a metaphor for political engagement and activism, one early example in the United States was the paramilitary youth organization the ___E:Wide Awakes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awakes)___ , which formed in ___E:Hartford, Connecticut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hartford,_Connecticut)___ , in 1860 to support the Republican candidate in the ___E:1860 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1860_United_States_presidential_election)___ , ___E:Abraham Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln)___ .
Local chapters of the group spread rapidly across northern cities in the ensuing months and "triggered massive popular enthusiasm" around the election.
The political militancy of the group also alarmed many southerners, who saw in the Wide Awakes confirmation of their fears of northern, Republican political aggression.

The support among the Wide Awakes for ___E:abolition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abolitionism_in_the_United_States)___ , as well as the participation of a number of black men in a Wide Awakes parade in Massachusetts, likely contributed to such anxiety.

One of the earliest uses of the idea of wokeness as a concept for black political consciousness came from Jamaican philosopher and social activist ___E:Marcus Garvey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Garvey)___ ,  who wrote in 1923, "Wake up Ethiopia!
Wake up Africa!"   In a collection of aphorisms published that year, Garvey expanded the metaphor: "Wake up Ethiopia!
Wake up Africa!
Let us work towards the one glorious end of a free, redeemed and mighty nation.

Let Africa be a bright star among the constellation of nations."   This sentiment was later echoed by singer ___E:Lauryn Hill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauryn_Hill)___ during her 2002 live album ___E:MTV Unplugged No. 2.0 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Unplugged_No._2.0)___ , where she urged listeners to "wake up and rebel".

Black American folk singer-songwriter Huddie Ledbetter, a.k.a. ___E:Lead Belly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_Belly)___ , used the phrase "stay woke" as part of a spoken afterword to a 1938 recording of his song "Scottsboro Boys", which tells the story of ___E:nine black teenagers and young men falsely accused of raping two white women U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsboro_Boys)___ in Alabama in 1931. In the recording, Lead Belly says he met with the defendant's lawyer and the young men themselves, and "I advise everybody, be a little careful when they go along through there ( ___E:Scottsboro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsboro,_Alabama)___ ) – best stay woke, keep their eyes open."   Aja Romano writes at ___E:Vox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vox_(website))___ that this usage reflects "black Americans' need to be aware of racially motivated threats and the potential dangers of white America."
By the mid-20th century, woke had come to mean 'well-informed' or 'aware',  especially in a political or cultural sense.

The Oxford English Dictionary traces the earliest such usage to a 1962 New York Times Magazine article titled "If You're Woke You Dig It" by African-American novelist ___E:William Melvin Kelley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Melvin_Kelley)___ , describing the appropriation of black slang by white ___E:beatniks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatnik)___ .

Woke had gained more political connotations by 1971 when the play Garvey Lives! by ___E:Barry Beckham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Beckham)___ included the line: "I been sleeping all my life. And now that Mr. Garvey done woke me up, I'm gon' stay woke. And I'm gon help him wake up other black folk."

Through the late 2000s and early 2010s, woke was used either as a term for literal ___E:wakefulness U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wakefulness)___ , or as slang for suspicions of ___E:infidelity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infidelity)___ .
The latter meaning was used in singer ___E:Childish Gambino U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Childish_Gambino)___ 's 2016 song " ___E:Redbone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redbone_(song))___ ".

In the 21st century's first decade, the use of woke encompassed the earlier meaning with an added sense of being "alert to social and/or ___E:racial discrimination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_discrimination)___ and injustice".

This usage was popularized by soul singer ___E:Erykah Badu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erykah_Badu)___ 's 2008 song " ___E:Master Teacher U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_Teacher_(Erykah_Badu_song))___ ",   via the song's refrain, "I stay woke".  ___E:Merriam-Webster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merriam-Webster)___ defines the expression stay woke in Badu's song as meaning, "self-aware, questioning the dominant paradigm and striving for something better"; and, although within the context of the song, it did not yet have a specific connection to justice issues, Merriam-Webster credits the phrase's use in the song with its later connection to these issues.

Songwriter ___E:Georgia Anne Muldrow U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Anne_Muldrow)___ , who composed "Master Teacher" in 2005, told ___E:Okayplayer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okayplayer)___ news and culture editor Elijah Watson that while she was studying jazz at ___E:New York University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University)___ , she learned the invocation Stay woke from Harlem alto saxophonist ___E:Lakecia Benjamin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakecia_Benjamin)___ , who used the expression in the meaning of trying to "stay woke" because of tiredness or boredom, "talking about how she was trying to stay up – like literally not pass out".

In homage, Muldrow wrote stay woke in marker on a T-shirt, which over time became suggestive of engaging in the process of the search for herself (as distinct from, for example, merely personal productivity).
According to The Economist , as the term woke and the #Staywoke hashtag began to spread online, the term "began to signify a progressive outlook on a host of issues as well as on race".

In a ___E:tweet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweet_(Twitter))___ mentioning the Russian feminist rock group ___E:Pussy Riot U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pussy_Riot)___ , whose members were imprisoned in 2012,   Badu wrote: "Truth requires no belief.
Stay woke. Watch closely. #FreePussyRiot".
This has been cited by Know Your Meme as one of the first examples of the #Staywoke hashtag.

Following the ___E:shooting of Michael Brown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_of_Michael_Brown)___ in 2014, the phrase stay woke was used by activists of the ___E:Black Lives Matter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter)___ (BLM) movement to urge awareness of police abuses.

The ___E:BET U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BET)___ documentary ___E:Stay Woke U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stay_Woke:_The_Black_Lives_Matter_Movement)___ , which covered the movement, aired in May 2016.  Within the decade of the 2010s, the word woke (the colloquial, ___E:passively voiced U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passively_voiced)___ past participle of wake ) obtained the meaning 'politically and socially aware'  among BLM activists.
While the term woke initially pertained to issues of racial prejudice and discrimination impacting African Americans, it came to be used by other activist groups with different causes.

While there is no single agreed-upon definition of the term, it came to be primarily associated with ideas that involve identity and race and which are promoted by progressives, such as the notion of ___E:white privilege U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_privilege)___ or ___E:slavery reparations for African Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reparations_for_slavery_in_the_United_States)___ .

According to communication studies scholar Gordana Lazić, woke refers to "a heightened awareness of social inequalities and injustices".  ___E:Vox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vox_(website))___ ' s Aja Romano writes that woke evolved into a "single-word summation of leftist political ideology, centered on social justice politics and ___E:critical race theory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critical_race_theory)___ ".
Columnist ___E:David Brooks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Brooks_(commentator))___ wrote in 2017 that "to be woke is to be radically aware and justifiably paranoid.

It is to be cognizant of the rot pervading the power structures."  Sociologist Marcyliena Morgan contrasts woke with ___E:cool U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cool_(aesthetic))___ in the context of maintaining dignity in the face of social injustice: "While coolness is empty of meaning and interpretation and displays no particular consciousness, woke is explicit and direct regarding injustice, racism, sexism, etc."

The term woke became increasingly common on ___E:Black Twitter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Twitter)___ , the community of African American users of the social media platform ___E:Twitter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter)___ .  ___E:André Brock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9_Brock)___ , a professor of black digital studies at the ___E:Georgia Institute of Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Institute_of_Technology)___ , suggested that the term proved popular on Twitter because its brevity suited the platform's 140-character limit.

According to Charles Pulliam-Moore, the term began crossing over into general internet usage as early as 2015.  The phrase stay woke became an ___E:Internet meme U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_meme)___ ,  with searches for woke on ___E:Google U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google)___ surging in 2015.

The term has gained popularity amid an increasing leftward turn on various issues among the ___E:American Left U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Left)___ ; this has partly been a reaction to the right-wing politics of U.S.

President ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ , who was elected in 2016, but also to a growing awareness regarding the extent of historical discrimination faced by African Americans.

According to Perry Bacon Jr., ideas that have come to be associated with "wokeness" include a rejection of ___E:American exceptionalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_exceptionalism)___ ; a belief that the United States has never been a true ___E:democracy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democracy)___ ; that people of color suffer from ___E:systemic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systemic_racism)___ and ___E:institutional racism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institutional_racism)___ ; that white Americans experience ___E:white privilege U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_privilege)___ ; that African Americans deserve reparations for slavery and post-enslavement discrimination; that disparities among racial groups, for instance in certain professions or industries, are automatic evidence of discrimination; that U.S. law enforcement agencies are designed to discriminate against people of color and so should be ___E:defunded U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defund_the_police)___ , ___E:disbanded U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abolish_the_police)___ , or heavily reformed; that women suffer from ___E:systemic sexism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systemic_sexism)___ ; that individuals should be able to identify with any ___E:gender U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender)___ or none; that U.S. ___E:capitalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitalism)___ is deeply flawed; and that Trump's election to the presidency was not an aberration but a reflection of the prejudices about people of color held by large parts of the U.S. population.

Although increasingly accepted across much of the American Left, many of these ideas were nevertheless unpopular among the U.S. population as a whole and among other, especially more ___E:centrist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centrist)___ , parts of the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ .

The term increasingly came to be identified with ___E:millennials U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennials)___  and members of ___E:Generation Z U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generation_Z)___ .  ___E:Les Echos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Echos_(France))___ lists woke among several terms adopted by Generation Z that indicate "a societal turning point" in France.
In May 2016, ___E:MTV News U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_News)___ identified woke as being among ten words teenagers "should know in 2016".

The ___E:American Dialect Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Dialect_Society)___ voted woke the slang word of the year in 2017.    In the same year, the term was included as an entry in Oxford English Dictionary .

By 2019, the term woke was increasingly being used in an ironic sense, as reflected in the books Woke by comedian ___E:Andrew Doyle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Doyle_(comedian))___ (using the pen name ___E:Titania McGrath U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titania_McGrath)___ ) and Anti-Woke by columnist ___E:Brendan O'Neill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brendan_O%27Neill_(columnist))___ .
By 2022, usage of the term had spread beyond the United States, attracting criticism by right-wing political figures in Europe.

By 2019,  opponents of progressive social movements were using the term mockingly or ___E:sarcastically U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcastic)___ ,   implying that "wokeness" was an insincere form of ___E:performative activism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performative_activism)___ .

Woke has been used ironically by the right wing to ridicule perceived left-wing " ___E:social justice warriors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_justice_warrior)___ " and " ___E:snowflakes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowflake_(slang))___ ", in connection with mockery of ___E:Millennials U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennials)___ and ___E:Gen Z U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen_Z)___ .

Author ___E:Sergio C. Fanjul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sergio_C._Fanjul&action=edit&redlink=1)___ [es] writes that some leftists, such as writer ___E:Daniel Bernabé U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Daniel_Bernab%C3%A9&action=edit&redlink=1)___ [es] and philosopher ___E:Susan Neiman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Neiman)___ , criticize wokeness as a form of tribalism which divides the working class and distracts from the universalist class struggle.

The term performative wokeness has been used to refer to social media activity perceived as a self-serving and superficial form of activism, i.e. " ___E:slacktivism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slacktivism)___ ".
British journalist ___E:Steven Poole U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Poole)___ comments that the term woke is used to mock "overrighteous liberalism".
This ___E:pejorative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pejorative)___ sense of woke means "following an intolerant and moralising ideology" according to The Economist .
As in the United States, the term woke is used by those on the political right wing in Canada to discredit individuals and policies they consider to be overly progressive.

During a debate in 2023 on the ___E:Law Society of Alberta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_Society_of_Alberta)___ 's 2020 adoption of a rule which made certain Continuing Professional Development (CPD) training courses on ___E:Indigenous Canadian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_Canadian)___ history obligatory, a lawyer from the ___E:Justice Centre for Constitutional Freedoms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice_Centre_for_Constitutional_Freedoms)___ wrote an op-ed arguing that the course was a form of "wokeness".   in the ___E:2025 Canada federal election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Canada_federal_election)___ , ___E:Conservative Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Party_of_Canada)___ leader ___E:Pierre Poilievre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Poilievre)___ ___E:weaponized U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weaponized)___ the term in his campaign, characterizing "social justice advocacy as an authoritarian threat".

Brazilian federal deputy ___E:Kim Kataguiri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Kataguiri)___ has accused the government ___E:under president Lula da Silva U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Lula_da_Silva)___ of promoting a "woke agenda" with a proposal to tax ___E:streaming services U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_service)___ and ___E:social media U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media)___ networks while requiring a certain amount of content to come from Brazilian companies with 51% of capital and shareholders belonging to "identity groups".  [better source needed]

Among ___E:American conservatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_conservatives)___ and ___E:centrists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centrism)___ , woke has come to be used primarily as an insult.

Members of the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ have been increasingly using the term to criticize members of the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ , while more centrist Democrats use it against more left-leaning members of their own party; such critics accuse those on their left of using ___E:cancel culture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancel_culture)___ to damage the employment prospects of those who are not considered sufficiently woke.   Perry Bacon Jr. suggests that this "anti-woke posture" is connected to a long-standing promotion of ___E:backlash U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backlash_(sociology))___ politics by the Republican Party, wherein it promotes white and conservative fear in response to activism by African Americans as well as changing cultural norms.
Such critics often believe that movements such as Black Lives Matter exaggerate the extent of social problems.
Among the uses by Republicans is the ___E:Stop WOKE Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_WOKE_Act)___ , a law that limits discussion of racism in Florida schools.

A program of eliminating books by LGBT and black authors from schools was conducted by the Florida government and by ___E:vigilantes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vigilantism)___ calling themselves "woke busters".

Florida governor and former presidential candidate ___E:Ron DeSantis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_DeSantis)___ has frequently used the term, referring to his state as a place "where woke goes to die."

Linguist and social critic ___E:John McWhorter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McWhorter)___ argues that the history of woke is similar to that of politically correct , another term once used self-descriptively by the left which was appropriated by the right as an insult, in a process similar to the ___E:euphemism treadmill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphemism_treadmill)___ .

Romano compares woke to canceled as a term for " 'political correctness' gone awry" among the American right wing.  Attacking the idea of wokeness, along with other ideas such as cancel culture and ___E:critical race theory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critical_race_theory)___ ,  became a large part of Republican Party electoral strategy.

Beginning in the ___E:first presidency of Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump)___ , commentators from the ___E:alt-right U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alt-right)___ , religious right, moderate liberals, and libertarians have attacked "woke" ideas and the " woke mind virus ", a phrase popularized by ___E:Elon Musk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk)___ , as existential threats to American society.

Trump stated in 2021 that the ___E:Biden administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biden_administration)___ was "destroying" the country "with woke", and Republican Missouri senator ___E:Josh Hawley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Hawley)___ used the term to promote his upcoming book by saying the "woke mob" was trying to suppress it.  According to USA Today , the term woke has been "co-opted by ___E:GOP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ activists".

By 2025, conservative commentators such as ___E:Rod Dreher U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_Dreher)___ and ___E:James A. Lindsay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_A._Lindsay)___ had begun using the term " woke right " to characterize far-right beliefs as a mirror of the far left.   Political commentator ___E:Jonathan Chait U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Chait)___ has described paleoconservative commentator ___E:Pat Buchanan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Buchanan)___ , who criticized the liberalism of the ___E:Obama era U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama_era)___ in a way that prefigured ___E:Trumpism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trumpism)___ , as the "godfather" of the "woke right".

Linguist John McWhorter writes that ___E:semantic broadening U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_broadening)___ of the term "woke" resulted in a shift in its meaning to "a conspiracy-focused and punitive orientation to social change", regardless of left–right orientation.

The term "woke right" has also been used by pro- ___E:Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ sources to describe American conservatives who became increasingly critical of Israel during the ___E:Gaza war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war)___ .

Following the ___E:assassination of Charlie Kirk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Charlie_Kirk)___ , right-wing activists and the U.S. government undertook a wide-reaching campaign to punish critics of Kirk for allegedly celebrating his death that soon turned into policing any criticism of Kirk or his ideology.

Author ___E:Jonathan Rauch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Rauch)___ of the ___E:Brookings Institution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brookings_Institution)___ has characterized it as a "woke right" campaign paralleling earlier efforts to suppress right-wing speech on college campuses.

In India, the term is used as a pejorative by ___E:Hindutva U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindutva)___ activists and ___E:Hindu nationalists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Nationalists)___ to refer to the critics of the Hindu nationalist ideology who are deemed as anti-Hindu by the Hindu nationalist organizations such as the ___E:Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashtriya_Swayamsevak_Sangh)___ .

The term is also synonymous with leftism in news headlines  and is commonly used in social media circles by critics of ___E:secularism in India U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secularism_in_India)___ .
In Hungary, politician ___E:Balázs Orbán U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bal%C3%A1zs_Orb%C3%A1n_(politician))___ stated that "we [Hungary] will not give up fighting against woke ideology".

In Switzerland, members of the youth wing of the right-wing populist ___E:Swiss People's Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_People%27s_Party)___ have criticized Swiss bank ___E:UBS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UBS)___ for its diversity policies, calling them "woke".

The phenomenon le wokisme (sometimes translated 'wokeism'  ) has also been used in ___E:French politics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_politics)___ to criticize ___E:anti-racist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-racist)___ movements and leftist scholarship, particularly since the ___E:2022 French presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_French_presidential_election)___ .
Much of the opposition to le wokisme sees it as an American import, incompatible with French values.

Mohamed Amer Meziane reported that then-education minister ___E:Jean-Michel Blanquer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Michel_Blanquer)___ , organized a conference at which he argued "woke" ideology "plots against the greatness of a white European civilization" and is therefore an "anti-Republican political religion".
Blanquer established an "anti-woke think tank" in opposition to what is perceived as an export from the English-speaking world.

This view also includes a conspiracy theory connecting "wokism" with pre-existing right-wing conspiracy theories of "Islamo-leftism", suggesting that leftists are manipulated by Islamists to ___E:replace European white-Christian civilization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Replacement_conspiracy_theory)___ with Islam.
In this context, "woke" is used pejoratively to describe progressive, anti-colonial, and anti-racist positions that are seen as incompatible with traditional French values.

According to French sociologist and political scientist ___E:Alain Policar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alain_Policar&action=edit&redlink=1)___ [fr] , woke originated from African American communities to describe awareness of ___E:social injustices U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination)___ and has been used pejoratively by French politicians from the former republican left, the right and the far right to label individuals engaged in ___E:anti-racist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-racist)___ , ___E:feminist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminist_movement)___ , ___E:LGBTQ U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_movements)___ , and ___E:environmental U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_movement)___ movements.
This derogatory usage gave rise to the noun wokisme , suggesting a homogeneous political movement propagating an alleged woke ideology.

French philosopher Pierre-Henri Tavoillot characterizes wokeism as a corpus of theories revolving around " ___E:identity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identity_politics)___ , ___E:gender U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender)___ and ___E:race U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(human_categorization))___ ", with the core principle of "revealing and condemning concealed forms of ___E:domination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_dominance_theory)___ ", positing that all aspects of society can be reduced to a "dynamic of oppressor and oppressed", with those oblivious to this notion deemed " ___E:complicit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complicity)___ ", while the "awakened ( woke )" advocate for the "abolition (cancel) of anything perceived to sustain such oppression", resulting in practical implementations such as adopting ___E:inclusive language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inclusive_language)___ , ___E:reconfiguring education U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_reform)___ or deconstructing ___E:gender norms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_norm)___ .
In the United Kingdom, anti-wokeness discourse is driven primarily by ___E:Conservative Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Party_(UK))___ politicians and right-wing media outlets.

Conservative papers such as The Daily Telegraph and Daily Mail commonly publish articles critical of what they deem to be woke. [citation needed] The Mail on Sunday publishes an annual "Woke List" criticising public figures for perceived " ___E:virtue signalling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtue_signalling)___ ".  [better source needed] The right-wing television channel ___E:GB News U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GB_News)___ was proclaimed at its founding to be explicitly anti-woke.  Its onetime chairman ___E:Andrew Neil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Neil)___ has presented a regular segment on the channel entitled "Wokewatch", which aims to be a counter-voice to "woke warriors".
The term woke is often used as a pejorative by conservative figures.

During the run-up to the ___E:2024 general election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_Kingdom_general_election)___ , the governing Conservative Party attracted criticism for attempting to create a ___E:culture war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_war)___ based on the woke concept.

While promoting her book The Abuse of Power in 2023, former Conservative prime minister ___E:Theresa May U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theresa_May)___ declared herself to be woke , in the sense of "somebody who recognizes that discrimination takes place".

In a survey by ___E:YouGov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouGov)___ , 73% of Britons who used the term said they did so in a disapproving way, 11% in an approving way and 14% neither used it in an approving or disapproving way.  Columnist ___E:Zoe Williams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoe_Williams_(writer))___ writes in The Guardian that public discourse around ___E:cycling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling)___ has become "the perfect microcosm of the wokeness split in all its forms", with anti-cycling voices portraying cyclists as a "lunatic fringe".

During the ___E:2022 Australian federal election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Australian_federal_election)___ campaign, both ___E:Scott Morrison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Morrison)___ , then-prime minister and leader of the centre-right ___E:Liberal Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_of_Australia)___ , and ___E:Anthony Albanese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Albanese)___ , the subsequently elected prime minister and leader of the centre-left ___E:Australian Labor Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Labor_Party)___ , insisted they were not "woke".

___E:Peter Dutton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Dutton)___ , former ___E:Opposition Leader U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leader_of_the_Opposition_(Australia))___ and leader of the Coalition, has also used the term several times before.

Members of minor right-wing parties, especially ___E:Pauline Hanson's One Nation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Hanson%27s_One_Nation)___ and the ___E:United Australia Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Australia_Party_(2013))___ , also frequently use the term. [citation needed]

In the ___E:2025 Australian federal election campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Australian_federal_election#Official_campaign)___ opposition leader Dutton stated that he wanted to rid the schooling and university system of "woke" policies.

In New Zealand, former deputy prime minister and leader of the ___E:New Zealand First Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_First_Party)___ , ___E:Winston Peters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Peters)___ , referred to the government led by ___E:Jacinda Ardern U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacinda_Ardern)___ and the ___E:New Zealand Labour Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Labour_Party)___ as a "woke guilt industry".
Then–opposition leader ___E:Judith Collins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judith_Collins)___ also referred to Ardern as "woke".

Scholars Michael B. McCormack and Althea Legal-Miller argue that the phrase stay woke echoes ___E:Martin Luther King Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr.)___ 's exhortation "to stay awake, to adjust to new ideas, to remain vigilant and to face the challenge of change".  [page needed]

Writer and activist ___E:Chloé Valdary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlo%C3%A9_Valdary)___ has stated that the concept of being woke is a "double-edged sword" that can "alert people to systemic injustice" while also being "an aggressive, performative take on progressive politics that only makes things worse".

Social-justice scholars Tehama Lopez Bunyasi and Candis Watts Smith, in their 2019 book Stay Woke: A People's Guide to Making All Black Lives Matter, argue against what they term as "Woker-than-Thou-itis: Striving to be educated around issues of social justice is laudable and moral, but striving to be recognized by others as a woke individual is self-serving and misguided."    Essayist Maya Binyam, writing in The Awl , ironized about a seeming contest among players who "name racism when it appears" or who disparage "folk who are lagging behind".  [further explanation needed]

Linguist ___E:Ben Zimmer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Zimmer)___ writes that, with mainstream currency, the term's "original grounding in African-American political consciousness has been obscured".

The Economist states that as the term came to be used more to describe white people active on social media, black activists "criticised the performatively woke for being more concerned with internet point-scoring than systemic change".

Journalist ___E:Amanda Hess U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Hess)___ says social media accelerated the word's ___E:cultural appropriation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_appropriation)___ ,  writing, "The conundrum is built in. When white people aspire to get points for consciousness, they walk right into the cross hairs between allyship and appropriation."   Hess describes woke as "the inverse of 'politically correct' ...
It means wanting to be considered correct, and wanting everyone to know just how correct you are".

In 2021, the British filmmaker and DJ ___E:Don Letts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Letts)___ suggested that "in a world so woke you can't make a joke", it was difficult for young artists to make protest music without being accused of ___E:cultural appropriation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_appropriation)___ .
By the mid-2010s, language associated with wokeness had entered the mainstream media and was being used for marketing.

Examples have included ___E:Nike's social-justice campaign featuring Colin Kaepernick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_Crazy)___ , a ___E:Pepsi advertisement featuring Kendall Jenner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_for_Now)___ , and ___E:Gillette's commentary on toxic masculinity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Best_Men_Can_Be)___ .

In 2018, African-American journalist ___E:Sam Sanders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Sanders_(journalist))___ argued that the authentic meaning of woke was being lost to overuse by white liberals and co-option by businesses trying to appear progressive ( woke-washing ), which would ultimately create a backlash.

The term woke capitalism was coined by writer ___E:Ross Douthat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Douthat)___ for brands that used politically progressive messaging as a substitute for genuine reform.
According to The Economist , examples of "woke capitalism" include advertising campaigns designed to appeal to millennials, who often hold more socially liberal views than earlier generations.

Abas Mirzaei, a senior lecturer in branding at ___E:Macquarie University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macquarie_University)___ , says brands "without a clear moral purpose" who use social-justice messages in advertising have been increasingly perceived as inauthentic, damaging the concept of wokeness and spawning the meme " ___E:get woke, go broke U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get_woke,_go_broke)___ ".

Cultural scientists Akane Kanai and ___E:Rosalind Gill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosalind_Gill)___ describe "woke capitalism" as the "dramatically intensifying" trend to include historically marginalized groups (currently primarily in terms of race, gender, and religion) as ___E:mascots U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mascot)___ in advertisement with a message of ___E:empowerment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empowerment)___ to signal progressive values.

On the one hand, Kanai and Gill argue that this creates an individualized and depoliticized idea of social justice, reducing it to an increase in self-confidence; on the other hand, the omnipresent visibility in advertising can also amplify a ___E:backlash U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backlash_(sociology))___ against the equality of precisely these minorities.

These would become mascots not only of the companies using them, but of the unchallenged ___E:neoliberal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoliberalism)___ economic system with its socially unjust order itself.

For the economically weak, the equality of these minorities would thus become indispensable to the maintenance of this economic system; the minorities would be seen responsible for the losses of this system.
